spans.s:
Ghora Āṅgirasa is the name of a mythical teacher in the kauṣītaki brāhmaṇa and the Chāndogya upaniṣad, where he is teacher of the strange kṛṣṇa devakīputra. That the name is certainly a mere figment is shown by the fact that this ‘dread descendant of the Aṅgirases’ has a counterpart in bhiṣaj ātharvaṇa, ‘the healing descendant of the Atharvans,’ while in the Rigveda Sūtras the Atharvāṇo vedaḥ is connected with bheṣajam and the Āṅgiraso vedaḥ with ghoram. He is accordingly a personification of the dark side of the practice of the Atharvaveda. He is also mentioned in the aśvamedha section of the kāṭhaka Saṃhitā.
Foot notes xxx. 6. Cf. Āśvalāyana śrauta Sütra, xii. 10.
